title: Antibiotic therapy in maxillofacial surgery in cases of documented penicillin allergy: a prospective multicenter study of a PEN-FAST-based delabeling and treatment concept with retrospective comparison group
summary:
Many patients have penicillin allergy listed in their medical records, although in most cases there is no real allergy. As a result, alternative antibiotics are often prescribed that are less effective and have more side effects. This study uses a simple assessment system (PEN-FAST score) to evaluate the actual risk of allergy.
Patients at low risk can receive a safe and effective antibiotic (cefazolin and metronidazole) and, if possible, undergo a short supervised test with amoxicillin to see if they are truly allergic. The results are compared with a previous group of patients who were treated without this procedure. The aim is to avoid unnecessary clindamycin prescriptions and improve the treatment of infections in the maxillofacial region.
conditions: Patients with odontogenic infection and a history of penicillin allergy

interventions.name:
Prospective implementation of a risk-adapted PEN-FAST-based therapy and delabeling workflow for inpatients undergoing maxillofacial surgery with a documented history of penicillin allergy.
If PEN-FAST <3, guideline-compliant antibiotic therapy with cefazolin + metronidazole is administered.
For PE

Pure observation of a retrospective cohort of maxillofacial surgery patients with documented penicillin allergy who were treated between 2023 and 2025 without the standardised risk-oriented PEN-FAST workflow.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Capable of giving consent, documented history of penicillin allergy (without proven/confirmed allergy), inpatient admission for surgical treatment of odontogenic infections
Exclusion criteria:
Unable to give consent, pregnancy or breastfeeding, severe immunosuppression, patients with confirmed penicillin allergy (e.g. diagnosed by an allergist)
